quality.method: Manual claim review against selected existing chunks, exact fallback answer comparison, six boundary equivalence checks over all 42 pairs; keyword tests supplement rather than replace review.
quality.rbac_definition: Grounded role/permission/database explanation. Preserves the essential definition and examples; no added world facts. 53 generated tokens, natural EOS.
quality.roles: Lists read, readWrite, dbAdmin, userAdmin and root from the document. Removes baseline mislabeling of readOnly and unsupported role/responsibility mixing. 26 generated tokens; question asks which roles, not a full permissions tutorial.
quality.indexing: Preserves creating/listing/dropping indexes and required permissions. Omits verbose examples and unrelated username discussion. 30 generated tokens including EOS, natural completion.
quality.all_other_cases: All 33 fallback answers are byte-identical to baseline, including refusals, quoted readWrite, accepted GRU/autoencoder definitions, temporal and implementation answers.
quality.known_baseline_limitations: GRU selected passages disagree: hidden-state formula uses (1-z) old + z candidate, while a numerical example treats z=0.9 as retaining 90% old state. The original implementation answer also mixes reset/update equations and reaches its 320-token cap. It remains byte-identical; this task does not certify it as factually correct.
quality.rejected_quality_candidates: Compact semantic schema changed RBAC/roles verdicts despite identical retrieved IDs and changed a GRU validation path. Initial short definition prompts lost reset-gate/reconstruction details and were reverted. Short implementation prompts mislabeled a reset-gate formula and were reverted.
quality.conclusion: No meaningful new regression in this frozen corpus. Absolute correctness of every legacy answer is not claimed.

semantic_output_observation.reason: Original outputs naturally terminate; lowering the cap alone does not save tokens. Rejected compact transport cannot justify a production cap change.

rag.question: According to this PDF, what is role-based access control?
rag.work_id: User Roles and Permissions in MongoDB
rag.answer: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is implemented in MongoDB where users can be assigned specific roles such as `read`, `readWrite`, and `dbAdmin` that grant them different levels of permissions including reading, writing, and administrative tasks on specified databases.
